hypothesis: A direct longest-path relaxation can resolve the finite taxi difference-constraint systems that generic sparse LP could not resolve within budget, yielding either a positive-cycle obstruction or a finite potential table.
rationale: The preceding five sparse LP models all timed out before returning a primal solution. Difference constraints have a specialized feasibility criterion: the system is feasible exactly when no directed cycle has positive total required potential increase. Integer relaxation can therefore provide an auditable certificate or a converged finite potential without introducing an objective, coefficient bounds, or a new candidate family.
expected_information_gain: A positive directed cycle would certify finite-graph infeasibility for the corresponding residual-edge exclusion pattern. Convergence would produce a table that can be independently checked on every frozen taxi edge and, only if it has fewer than three violations after the audit, sent to the primary evaluator. A wall/pass limit remains inconclusive and closes the route operationally after this one rescue.
method: Load the pinned circle_taxi_k4_m6 metric, convert the exact integer edge weights w=ext-(k+1)d_min, and run synchronous longest-path relaxation with one integer potential variable per node, initialized at zero. Run exactly the same five models as the LP diagnostic: no residual edge removed, each residual pair removed, and all three removed. Stop on convergence, on the first pass reaching 166,681 iterations (the finite positive-cycle criterion), or at the 1,800-second total wall limit. Reconstruct and integer-check any positive cycle from predecessor edges; save any converged potential with the complete node work-function table. No taxi or primary-evaluator follow-up is performed until an independent all-edge audit.
metric: frozen circle-taxi violations_k under the identical edge inequality; target is violations_k < 3
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A positive-cycle certificate is only a finite benchmark obstruction. A finite table with a count below 3 is a strict improvement only for the pinned evaluator; arbitrary node values do not establish a general k-server potential or prove the conjecture.

configuration.variable_definition: one integer scalar per frozen taxi node/work-function row
configuration.relaxation: synchronous longest-path Bellman-Ford update from zero super-source
configuration.certificate: positive cycle in the retained directed graph
configuration.integer_weight_check: all edge weights must equal their rounded integer values

compute_budget.cpu: Windows pinned upstream runtime with Numba-compiled integer relaxation
compute_budget.memory_intent: edge arrays and two node vectors; no evaluator or metric changes

kill_condition: Stop after the five declared models, convergence, a positive-cycle certificate, 166,681 passes, or the 1,800-second wall limit. Do not add edge exclusions, alternate update orders, floating tolerances, or solver formulations after seeing results. If no model yields a certificate or converged potential within budget, close arbitrary finite-potential fitting as computationally unproductive.

raw_result.circle_control: not_validly_evaluated: taxi-only table covers 105 of 1001 circle nodes; combined primary attempt preserved as failure

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: only a full frozen taxi count below 3 is strict finite improvement

previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: this is a deterministic feasibility diagnostic, not a generalizing candidate family

interpretation: The direct integer relaxation converged for all five declared systems. The no-removal table was independently checked on all 7,000,602 frozen taxi edges with zero violations and then passed the unchanged pinned primary evaluator on the taxi target with violations_k=0. This is a strict improvement for the frozen finite evaluator only: the table is an arbitrary per-node artifact, did not validly cover the complete-circle metric, and was not robustness- or generalization-verified.
what_was_learned: The published three-violation canonical candidate is not an obstruction of the finite taxi graph when arbitrary node-indexed potentials are allowed. The graph admits an integer potential satisfying every frozen taxi inequality, but the cross-metric audit shows that this table does not define a transferable k-server potential.
recommended_next_action: Treat the zero-violation table as a finite evaluator witness, not a proof. Spend at most one bounded structural-extraction diagnostic seeking a compact work-function rule that reproduces the table or transfers to the circle metric; if it fails, close k-server search and retain the finite witness with its limitations.
repetition_justification: This is an algorithmically distinct exact difference-constraint relaxation and certificate method, not a rerun of the generic sparse LP solver; it uses the same frozen inequalities and declared exclusions to resolve the prior computational limit.
